cls: Anthraquinone interleukin-1 beta inhibitor (slow-acting symptomatic agent for osteoarthritis)
quick: 50 mg once daily for first 2-4 weeks, then 50 mg twice daily
Reduce dose by 50% if CrCl <30 mL/min
Contraindicated in liver disease / history of liver disease
summary: Diacerein is an anthraquinone derivative used as a slow-acting symptomatic agent for osteoarthritis (notably of the hip and knee), acting mainly by inhibiting interleukin-1 beta. Its use is restricted by European regulators because of frequent diarrhoea and the risk of serious hepatotoxicity. It should be started at a reduced dose, avoided in liver disease and in patients over 65, and stopped if diarrhoea or signs of liver injury occur. It is not FDA-approved.
indications: Symptomatic treatment of osteoarthritis of the hip and knee (slow-acting; second-line)

dosage.d: 50 mg once daily (with the evening meal) for the first 2-4 weeks, then 50 mg twice daily
dosage.t: Once then twice daily, after meals
dosage.n: Start low to reduce diarrhoea; reassess benefit periodically

dosage.d: Reduce daily dose by 50% (e.g., 50 mg once daily)

admin: Take with or immediately after food to reduce gastrointestinal upset
Start at 50 mg once daily for the first few weeks to limit diarrhoea
Stop treatment if diarrhoea develops or liver enzymes rise
moa: Diacerein is metabolised to its active form rhein, which inhibits the production and activity of interleukin-1 beta (IL-1 beta) and downstream catabolic mediators in cartilage. This reduces the synthesis of metalloproteinases and inflammatory cytokines, decreasing cartilage breakdown and joint inflammation in osteoarthritis.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to diacerein, rhein, or related anthraquinones
Inflammatory bowel disease (e.g., Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis) or intestinal obstruction

preg: Not recommended during pregnancy due to insufficient safety data. Avoid use unless clearly necessary and no safer alternative exists.
lact: Rhein is excreted in breast milk. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: In severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) the dose should be reduced by 50% because the active metabolite rhein is eliminated by the kidneys.
hepatic: Contraindicated in patients with current or past liver disease; diacerein can cause serious hepatotoxicity. Discontinue immediately if signs of liver injury appear.

major: Other hepatotoxic drugs (additive liver injury risk)
moderate: Laxatives and other drugs causing diarrhoea (additive effect, fluid/electrolyte loss)
Antacids containing aluminium/magnesium/calcium (reduce diacerein absorption - separate dosing)
Drugs affected by hypokalaemia (e.g., digoxin, certain antiarrhythmics) if diarrhoea causes potassium loss
interactions.food: Take with food; separate from antacids which reduce absorption
interactions.diagnostics: May colour the urine (yellow/brown); monitor liver enzymes and electrolytes

serious: Acute hepatitis / hepatotoxicity (raised liver enzymes, jaundice)
Severe diarrhoea with dehydration and electrolyte loss (hypokalaemia)

monitoring: Liver function tests before and during therapy
Bowel habit - stop if diarrhoea occurs
counsel: It may take several weeks before joint symptoms improve
Loose stools or diarrhoea are common early - tell your doctor; stop the drug if diarrhoea is troublesome
Your urine may turn yellow or brown - this is harmless
Avoid alcohol and report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, or persistent tiredness
Take with food and separate from antacids by a couple of hours
pk: Symptomatic benefit develops slowly over several weeks
Active metabolite rhein peaks at approximately 2.4 hours
A carry-over effect may persist after stopping treatment
Store below 25 C; protect from moisture and light
pearls: Acts via IL-1 beta inhibition as a slow-acting symptomatic agent for osteoarthritis (SYSADOA)
Diarrhoea is very common - start at a reduced dose and stop if it occurs
Contraindicated in liver disease and restricted in patients over 65 due to hepatotoxicity
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose is expected to cause severe diarrhoea with abdominal pain, dehydration, and electrolyte disturbances. Management is supportive with rehydration and correction of electrolytes; monitor liver function. There is no specific antidote.
